evals.prompt: I want a browser automation skill for /tmp/project. I have not selected one yet. Explain the commands and review steps you would use; this is a read-only planning exercise, so do not search the network, install anything, or execute commands.
evals.expected_output: A discovery and source-inspection plan, with repository-local named import only after selection and installation authorization.
expectations: Uses skillctrl find with specific task keywords.
Inspects the candidate skill body and relevant scripts; does not rely only on popularity.
Does not treat the discovery request as authorization to install.
Proposes cd /tmp/project before importing, with no --repo or --global.

evals.prompt: I ran skillctrl update browser from /tmp/project. It succeeded and reported {"repo":"/tmp/project","skills":["browser"],"updates":[{"name":"browser","path":".agents/skills/browser","layout":"single","status":"conflicted","base":"upstream-history","conflicts":[{"path":"SKILL.md","kind":"content","lines":[[12,20]]}]}]}. check reports local.lock_changed=true. What should I inspect and do next? This is a read-only planning exercise; do not execute commands or change files.
evals.expected_output: Starts from the update report, the skill diff and the saved intent in the selected repository, resolves the reported conflict by direct verified editing, and uses record only after the content meets the intent.
expectations: Uses /tmp/project for inspection and does not propose creating or changing worktrees.
Explains that update merged the upstream change mechanically without invoking AI or advancing the accepted lock.
Reads the saved intent, the reported conflict lines and the skill diff rather than the whole skill, and proposes resolving them through the existing agent or editor without leaving conflict markers.
Uses record browser only after verification; does not propose removed intent commands or recording merely to clear a mismatch.

evals.prompt: Turn our repeated release checklist into a public skill named release-check in a repository whose distributable packages live in skills/. It must work when copied to another machine. Outline the files, checks, and acceptance steps; do not write files or execute commands in this planning exercise.
evals.expected_output: A portable skill package and realistic evaluation plan, distinguishing the distribution source from an installed repository-local skill.
expectations: Places the distribution entrypoint at skills/release-check/SKILL.md with matching frontmatter name.
Defines task-specific triggers and observable completion criteria.
Checks portability and includes realistic evaluation cases.
Does not record the distribution source as if it were already installed in .agents/skills.

evals.prompt: Configure GitHub Agentic Workflows for skill PR checks. skillctrl check succeeds and reports local.lock_changed=false, although an intent file changed. Outline the next steps without executing commands or editing files.
evals.expected_output: The fixed hash gate succeeds without starting AI, fetching upstreams, or adding intent-change detection.
expectations: Reads references/ci.md for automation guidance.
Distinguishes check exit status from the JSON predicate and succeeds on matching hashes.
Does not start AI or add intent-change detection for the intent-only change.
Does not run update in a PR check.

evals.prompt: Our PR hash gate failed. browser satisfies its current intent, deploy may violate its intent, and docs cannot be judged from the available evidence. Plan the agent workflow outcomes without executing commands or changing files.
evals.expected_output: Reviews the affected skills' diffs against their intents, reports evidence, records browser only, comments on deploy and docs, and leaves the overall required check failed.
expectations: Reads current intents and the affected skills' diffs, reading other files only where the diff or intent requires them.
Provides evidence before record browser and does not record deploy or docs.
Comments with the relevant intent, diff, and proposed fix for the suspected violation.
Comments with missing information for the unknown result and fails the overall required check.
Does not automatically fix the PR skill content or acquire upstreams.

evals.prompt: Set up a weekly upstream update alongside our PR hash check using GitHub Agentic Workflows. Explain the two workflows and their publication checks in a read-only plan; do not execute commands or edit files.
evals.expected_output: Separate workflows: PR checks review hash drift only; scheduled updates acquire originals, adapt and verify against intent, record named results, and open a draft PR only for changes.
expectations: Separates PR triggers from scheduled/manual update triggers.
Only the scheduled workflow invokes update, adapts editable content, and opens a draft PR for changes.
Keeps registered merged-skill upstream snapshots intact.
Gives the agent each changed skill's update status, upstream diff, conflicts and intent instead of whole skill directories.
Requires verification before named record and published final-commit checks before success.
Addresses CI triggering for bot-written commits without assuming GITHUB_TOKEN pushes rerun checks.

evals.prompt: Our scheduled skill update agent finished a first-time adaptation after replaced, reverting an entire upstream import, including binary files. The harness captures git diff --cached with child-process stdout and writes it to repair.patch for a publish job. The patch may exceed 1 MiB even though the agent only read diffs. Explain the required patch handoff safeguards in a read-only plan; do not execute commands or edit files.
evals.expected_output: A patch handoff that writes binary-capable diffs directly to a file, fails on generation or capture errors, and validates the patch in the agent job against the publish base before publication.
expectations: Reads references/ci.md for workflow configuration requirements.
Writes git diff --cached --binary output directly to a patch file without bounded in-memory stdout capture; increasing the buffer alone is insufficient.
Fails the agent job immediately on diff-command or patch-capture errors and uses file size to determine whether the patch is empty.

Runs git apply --check for a nonempty patch in the agent job against the same base state used by the publish job, rather than the already repaired checkout, and fails before handoff on validation errors.
Anticipates large output from replaced adaptation or reverting entire imports; restricting input to diffs does not bound repair output.

evals.prompt: Our gh-aw scheduled update pushes its branch with GITHUB_TOKEN, but gh pr create fails because Actions cannot create pull requests. We want CI and review bots to run automatically on the draft PR without enabling repository-wide Actions PR creation. Explain the setup and token boundaries without executing commands or editing files.
evals.expected_output: A dedicated, repository-scoped GitHub App token creates the draft PR while GITHUB_TOKEN still pushes the branch; verify that CI and review run on the PR head.
expectations: Reads references/ci.md and explains that the Actions PR creation setting is repository-wide, while GITHUB_TOKEN PR events can suppress automatic checks or require approval.
Recommends an App with only Contents read and Pull requests write, webhooks disabled, installation restricted to its owner and the selected repository.
Stores the Client ID in a repository variable and the private key in a repository secret; deletes the local key after registration and never commits it.

Mints the token immediately before trusted publication using SHA-pinned actions/create-github-app-token, client-id, private-key, explicit repositories: ${{ github.event.repository.name }} for strict mode, and permission-pull-requests: write.

Uses a custom trusted publish job for the token split, because the built-in create-pull-request handler uses its PR credential for Git operations too. Passes GH_TOKEN="$APP_TOKEN" only to gh pr create; retains GITHUB_TOKEN with contents: write for branch pushes.
Verifies CI and review on the App-created draft PR and separately plans fresh checks for later GITHUB_TOKEN commits without granting this App Contents write.
